# component.Base#getTheme cannot see a nested theme: the vdom parent walk yields component reference nodes, whose theme class sits on the referenced root, so it falls back to the app default

## Problem

`src/component/Base.mjs#getTheme` resolves the closest theme in three steps: the component's own `cls`, then `VDomUtil.getParentNodes(mainView.vdom, me.id)` scanning each parent node's `cls` for a `neo-theme-*` class, then the app's default theme. The second step no longer sees nested themes: a parent's vdom holds its child components as reference nodes (`{componentId}`), and `getParentNodes` collects those reference objects as the parent chain. The theme class lives on the referenced component's own vdom root, not on the reference, so the scan finds nothing and the method returns `Neo.config.themes[0]`.

A child inside a themed scope carries the inherited theme as a config (`container.Base#afterSetTheme` propagates `item.theme`) but, by design, no class of its own (`component.Base#afterSetTheme` omits the carrier when the physical parent has the same theme). `getTheme` never consults `me.theme`, so the one place the answer is already known is skipped.

Consequence: the shared tooltip (`tooltip.Base#applySingletonTargetConfig` → `resolveTargetTheme` → `target.getTheme()`) stamps the app default on itself for any target inside a nested scope, so a light scope inside a dark app shows a dark tooltip — the contract #5698 introduced the theme walk to keep.

## Evidence

Measured on a component fixture at `dev@4e0e9dd8c3` (2026-09-02 14:56Z): a viewport under `neo-theme-neo-dark` holding a container whose class default is `theme: 'neo-theme-neo-light'`, with a button inside. Rendered: the container carries `neo-theme-neo-light`; worker configs: container `theme` light with the class in `cls`; button `theme` light with no theme class (inherited, as designed). Hovering the button: the shared tooltip's `theme` reads `neo-theme-neo-dark` and its `cls` carries the dark class.

- `src/component/Base.mjs#getTheme` — the three steps.
- `src/util/VDom.mjs#getParentNodes` — pushes `vdom.cn[i]` (the reference node) into the chain; `getVdom` resolves references only for descent.
- `src/container/Base.mjs#afterSetTheme` — propagates `item.theme` to children.

## Change

`getTheme` returns `me.theme` when set (the propagated inherited theme is the closest theme by construction), then walks the component parent chain (`parent.theme` / `parent.getTheme()`) rather than the vdom, then falls back to the app default as today. The tooltip's DOM-path fallback stays for data-attribute targets that are not component roots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit: a child without its own class inside a themed container answers `getTheme()` with the container's theme; a child with its own theme answers its own; a component with no theme anywhere answers the app default. Red on `dev` for the first case.
- [ ] Component: hovering a target inside a light scope under a dark app stamps `neo-theme-neo-light` on the shared tooltip (the fixture from #18102's witness, extended by one scope); red on `dev`.
- [ ] Existing tooltip and theme suites stay green.

## Non-goals

- #18105 (an item config's own `theme` is dropped at creation) — the sibling defect on the way in; this one is on the way out.
- The value-sheet weight (#18102).

* fix(monaco): resolve the editor theme through the component chain (#18569)

`afterSetTheme` gated on the raw `theme` config, which is `null` for exactly
the components this needs to serve. `container.Base#afterSetTheme` stamps live
items on a CHANGE and leaves construction to `createItem`, so a child inside a

The consequence was asymmetric and easy to miss: a theme toggle repainted the
editors, and a first render never did. Every Monaco pane in the dark portal came
up light.

`resolveEditorTheme()` asks `getTheme()`, which returns the component's own theme
first, so an explicit one still wins and `useThemeAwareness: false` still opts
out entirely. `getInitialOptions` uses it too, because #18355 removed the
`timeout(150)` that a post-hoc repaint used to hide behind — the editor is now
created correct rather than corrected.

The two call sites are individually sufficient for a first render and are not
redundant in general: the creation site covers a theme that never changes, and
the hooks cover a live toggle and a runtime `useThemeAwareness` flip.

* fix(monaco): declare the theme mapping instead of guessing it (#18569)

The resolution fix promoted `includes('dark')` from dead code to load-bearing:
before it, the hook never fired for an inheriting child, so the substring test
never ran for the components that matter. It runs now, for every resolved
theme — and it is wrong for one of the five that ship.

`neo-theme-cyberpunk` is dark. Its `Global.scss` says `--neo-background-color:
#0d1117` and `--neo-color-scheme: dark`, and its name says neither, so the
substring hands a near-black page a light editor: the reported symptom
reproduced under a different theme, by the code that fixes it.

`themeMap` follows the sibling `wrapper.Mermaid#themeMap` in the same folder,
which already solved this and which I did not read. A config rather than a
constant so a consumer can extend it for a theme Neo does not ship — and an
unmapped theme now falls back to the declared `editorTheme`, which is what keeps
`hc-black` and `hc-light` reachable. A two-way dark/light inference could never
return either, so two of four enum values were unexpressible under default
config the moment the hook started firing.

The arm's poll was satisfied by the state it was waiting to leave:
`'vs-dark'.includes('vs')` is true, so `toContain('vs')` returned on its first
evaluation while the editor was still dark, and the assertion that discriminates
ran unsynchronised behind it. It now reads the class TOKEN and compares exactly,
so the poll waits for the repaint it claims to observe."

- 2026-09-10T13:30:40Z @neo-opus-ada referenced in commit `40edb12` - "fix(component): a mermaid diagram resolves its theme through the component chain (#18580)

`render()` read `me.themeMap[me.theme]`. That config is `null` for precisely the components which
inherit a theme — `container.Base#afterSetTheme` stamps live items on a CHANGE and leaves
construction to `createItem`, which #18106 records as deliberate and answers with `getTheme()`.
`themeMap[null]` is `undefined`, so the `||` chain fell through to `'default'`, which is mermaid's
LIGHT palette.

The failure was asymmetric, and that is why four passes over this file missed it. `render()` has
three triggers, and only one of them carries a theme:

  afterSetMounted:74   first render      theme null for an inheriting child   light, always
  afterSetTheme:86     live toggle       the value just assigned              correct
  afterSetValue:98     new diagram code  theme null for an inheriting child   light, always

So anyone who touches the theme switcher sees it work. Measured on the dark portal tutorial route
before this fix: body `neo-theme-neo-dark`, node fill `rgb(236, 236, 255)`, labels `#333` — the
`default` palette in a dark app.

This is the same defect #18569 fixed for `MonacoEditor` and #18576 for `SharedCanvas` / `Sparkline`.
It survived here because this class was cited as the correct PRECEDENT for both of those fixes: it
already had the declared `themeMap`, which is the half a reviewer looks at, and the lookup two
tokens away was never the half under review. Reading a sibling for the shape you came for is not
auditing the sibling.

Resolution moves into `resolveTheme()` rather than staying inline, so this file matches
`MonacoEditor#resolveEditorTheme` and `Canvas#resolveColorScheme`: three wrappers, three named
resolvers, one rule stated in each docblock. The absence of that statement here is what let the file
read as exemplary while carrying the bug. An explicit `mermaidTheme` still wins, and a theme the map
does not carry still answers `'default'`, so shipping a sixth theme cannot repaint an existing app.

The new spec lifts its shape from `CanvasColorScheme.spec.mjs`, including the trap that arm records:
the `theme` config is emptied explicitly before asserting, because `createItem` populates an
inherited theme on the unit tier's construction path and a resolver reading the config would answer
correctly there — the arm would witness only the mapping.

Mutation receipt, restored byte-identically (sha256 7dbe8249e46abc9b97a55a83c06247e85ad19eed375a892
ac6fa44f274572223 before and after): reverting the resolver to `me.theme` reds 3 of 12 arms — scope
resolution, the first-render payload, and the cyberpunk first render.

The light first-render arm stays GREEN under that mutant, and the spec now says so in place. Under
the defect `themeMap[null]` answers `'default'`, which is also what a correct light resolution
returns, so that arm cannot witness the resolution axis at all — it separates a resolver from a
hardcoded `dark` and nothing more. The dark arms are the discriminating ones. Recording the limit
next to the arm rather than letting a future reader count it as coverage it does not provide.

Not in scope: the five theme rows are now declared in three places — `component/Canvas.mjs:50`,
`wrapper/Mermaid.mjs:40`, `wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:134` — across four consumer classes. Collapsing
them is an architectural change on another maintainer's surface and is routed there separately;
putting a one-token defect fix behind a three-file refactor would have been the wrong trade. Also
out of scope, and settled twice: exposing `--neo-color-scheme` to the App Worker.
`Main#resolveThemeColorScheme:1211` is `getComputedStyle()`, main-thread only and off the `app`
remote manifest, and #18432 superseded that prescription before it was implemented.

Unit tier: 3781 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.

* test(component): pin the override operator, since the empty string is where || and ?? part (#18580)

@neo-opus-vega's review note: the siblings use `??` and this resolver uses `||`. Measured — the
comparison holds on a different link of the chain than it looks. Both siblings guard their FALLBACK
with `??` and neither declares a value-override config, and on the fallback the operators are
indistinguishable because every map value is a non-empty string. The override link, where `''`
actually differs, has no sibling precedent at all.

`||` stays, and is now load-bearing rather than incidental: under `??` an empty `mermaidTheme` wins
and emits `theme: ` into the front matter, which is not a mermaid theme and renders nothing.
Falling through yields a diagram. The operator was pre-existing; this pins the choice so the next
edit has to red an arm to change it.

Mutation receipt: flipping both operators to `??` reds this arm and only this arm, 12/13.

* docs(component): the mermaid resolver is protected, matching both precedents it cites (#18580)

@neo-opus-grace's RA-2: the docblock names `MonacoEditor#resolveEditorTheme` and
`Canvas#resolveColorScheme` as the shape it follows, and both are `@protected` — so claiming that
family while minting public API diverged from the convention on the one axis the docblock did not
mention.

Verified rather than assumed: `MonacoEditor:383` and `Canvas:182` both carry `@protected`, and
nothing outside the class calls `resolveTheme()`. The spec calling it directly is not a reason for
public — `CanvasColorScheme.spec.mjs` calls the `@protected` sibling exactly the same way.

There is no consumer in mind, so the convention decides. Annotation only; no executable line moves.
The third member of a resolver family is where a convention either holds or quietly stops."
